title: Who's really private?
description:
Here's a talk description for "Who's really private?":

Who's really private?
20 minutes

We say we care about privacy. We install ad blockers, complain about tracking, and nod along to every headline about data breaches. And yet we trade our location, our contacts, our purchase history, and our faces for things as small as a loyalty discount or a slightly faster checkout. This talk starts from that contradiction: not "why don't people care about privacy?" but "what does our behaviour actually reveal about what we value?"

Drawing on examples from everyday consumer tech, social platforms, and the promises made by "privacy-first" products (including ones built on blockchains), this talk looks at the gap between stated preference and revealed preference — and why that gap is wider and more consistent than most privacy advocates want to admit.
